// Safe polymorphic JSON field normalization (BroadcastPayload.go)
func normalizeJSONField(value interface{}, label string) (interface{}, error) {
    switch v := value.(type) {
    case string:
        var decoded interface{}
        if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(v), &decoded); err != nil {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to unmarshal %s: %w", label, err)
        }
        return decoded, nil
    case map[string]interface{}, []interface{}:
        return v, nil
    default:
        return v, nil
    }
}

��## API: Save Personalization Onboarding Answers

Related frontend flow: panorra-pwa#3223. Database migration is tracked separately in #417.

Implementation

  • Added authenticated POST /users/onboarding.
  • Only user sessions are allowed; viewer sessions receive 401.
  • Supports partial saves so each onboarding screen can persist its field without overwriting earlier answers.
  • Stores and returns: discovery_source, place_interests, usage_intent, onboarding_completed, and onboarding_completed_at.
  • Validates enum values, requires at least one interest, and deduplicates interests while preserving order.
  • Allows completion only when all required onboarding answers exist.
  • Supports the established encrypted response format when ec: true is supplied.

Request Contract

{
  "discovery_source": "social_media",
  "place_interests": ["nature_scenery", "food_markets"],
  "usage_intent": "plan_trip",
  "completed": true,
  "ec": true
}

Allowed values:

Field Allowed values
discovery_source social_media, friend_or_family, search_engine, blog_or_article, event_or_community, other
place_interests attractions, nature_scenery, history_heritage, culture_local_life, food_markets, hotels_stays, events_venues, architecture_unique_places
usage_intent explore_virtually, find_near_me, plan_trip, discover_hidden_gems, preview_venue_property, upload_share_360

Intended Behavior

  • Omitted fields do not clear saved answers.
  • completed: true marks onboarding complete only after the required answers are available.
  • completed: false must not reset completed onboarding. It is a valid no-op request.
  • onboarding_completed_at is set server-side.

QA Summary - 13 August 2026

Verdict: BUG CONFIRMED. The explicit valid no-op request completed: false is rejected with 400.

Confirmed Coding Defect

Item Result
Endpoint POST /users/onboarding
Expected Accept completed: false without resetting the saved completion state.
Actual Dev result 400 Required Input Body / Nothing to save
Root cause completed: false does not add an update; the handler then treats the request as empty and rejects it.
Impact A client explicitly sending the valid non-completion state receives an erroneous validation error.

  • Root Cause Analysis (Issue #416 Retest):
    • Previously on 13 August 2026, clients sending {"completed": false} received HTTP 400 Bad Request ("Required Input Body" / "Nothing to save"). The legacy handler only added to updates when completed == true, leading len(updates) == 0 to trigger an empty payload rejection.

      • Implemented HasOnboardingInput(completed *bool, updateCount int) bool: 
        func HasOnboardingInput(completed *bool, updateCount int) bool {
    return completed != nil || updateCount > 0
}
      • In SaveOnboarding.go, lines 99–107 check if !HasOnboardingInput(request.Completed, len(updates)). If only completed: false is provided, validation passes, no redundant DB update is fired (len(updates) == 0), and the current saved state is retrieved and returned with HTTP 200 OK.
    2. Enum Validation & Deduplication:
      • ValidateDiscoverySource: Checks against 6 whitelisted sources.
      • ValidatePlaceInterests: Requires at least one interest and deduplicates while preserving order.
      • ValidateUsageIntent: Checks against 6 whitelisted intents.
    3. Automated Unit & Regression Tests:
